Owner digests#

This page shows how an owner who asks gets a digest of only their own apps. Next: metrics.

A digest is a short note in plain words: what changed in that owner's apps since the previous scan, then where each app stands. Nothing changed, no digest. Nobody gets one by default, and Rollcall never guesses an owner from commit authors.

1. Say who answers for which apps#

Keep an owners file outside git (it names apps and contacts, so it is internal, like .env) and point ROLLCALL_OWNERS_FILE at it. An owner opts in with "digest": true; leaving the key out means no.

{
    "owners": [
        {"contact": "team@example.test", "digest": true, "projects": ["group/project", "group/other-project"]},
        {"contact": "another-team@example.test", "projects": ["group/third-project"]}
    ]
}

Here the first team gets digests and the second does not. A contact is a mail address or a team alias; each one is listed once. The shape is contract/owners.schema.json.

2. Print them#

After a scan:

rollcall digest

prints one digest per opted-in owner with news, each headed To: and Subject:. --owner=CONTACT picks one owner (an owner who has not opted in is refused), --format=json gives a script the same digests (contract/digest.schema.json), and --out=DIR writes them as <scan date>-<contact>.txt instead of printing, for a mail tool you already run. A line on stderr counts how many owners had news and how many get nothing this time.

What counts as a change, app by app:

  • the PHP image moved (a move from end of life to a supported PHP says so, with a well-earned "Present!");
  • the declared PHP floor, the Laravel version or the PROCTOR result changed;
  • a drift flag appeared ("now runs an end-of-life Laravel") or cleared ("no longer has a failing PROCTOR result"), including one that appears because a date in CREED's policy passed;
  • an app answered present for the first time, or was in the last scan and is not in this one.

The first scan has no "before", so the first digest is a first roll call: every app and where it stands. The states and flags are the report's own (rollcall report --internal), so a digest and the report never disagree.

3. Mail them (only if you want Rollcall to)#

Sending is a second, separate switch, and every part of it must be there:

  1. composer require symfony/mailer (Rollcall only suggests it).
  2. ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_ENABLED=true.
  3. ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_DSN: a Symfony Mailer DSN, such as smtp://mail.example.test:25. It can hold a password, so it is a secret: never in git, never printed.
  4. ROLLCALL_DIGEST_MAIL_FROM: the from address.
  5. rollcall digest --send.

Without any one of them nothing is mailed; with the settings but no --send, the digests are only printed. Every contact with news must be a mail address, or nothing goes out at all. Mail is plain text. This is the one outbound action in Rollcall, so it stays behind both the flag and the settings.

Schedule it right after rollcall scan: weekly suits the burn-down, and a quiet week sends nothing.
